regime_context: The detector shows a broad (51% eligible), non-one-narrative structure with Memory/HBM & Storage as the leader over AI Infrastructure (margin 0.595), but rotation.timing has no validated forward edge and cross-sectional rank-IC is ~0 — so this is a leadership/focus read, not a return forecast. gate_helps is true, so the absolute-trend discipline IS a valid staying-power/risk leg here, which permits slightly more than a whisper on eligible trend-healthy themes, but the guardrails cap confidence. Macro backdrop is coincident AI/geopolitics headline flow with 100% unscheduled share — noisy, no trigger.
emerging_watch: Watching whether AI Infrastructure (rank 2, score 1.745, uncrowded) CONFIRMS a leadership handoff from Memory/HBM: the observable condition would be AI Infrastructure closing the 0.595 margin to within ~0.2 AND holding eligibility for >5 sessions in a row. Until that confirmation, this is a watch only — leadership is still with Memory.

theses.subject: Memory, HBM & Storage
theses.thesis: The rank-1 position is supported by the ONLY validated leg that matters here — trend-gate eligibility is true and gate_helps is true, so de-risking into this theme respects the one actionable edge. Durability (0.68) and breadth (0.75) are healthy, and it is NOT crowded (z=0.53). This is a staying-power / de-risk lean, not a momentum-chasing call — I am deliberately ignoring the top rank as a return signal per guardrails.
theses.dissent: Hurﬆ_tag is 'mixed', not 'trend' — the price path lacks a clean persistent trend signature, so the 'staying power' justification is thinner than for a full trend tag. A memory cycle unwind (e.g. DRAM/NAND spot pricing rolls over) would cut this regardless of trend-gate logic.

falsifier.text: SMH/Storage complex trends below its 20-week average before the 30-day check-by.

theses.subject: Cybersecurity
theses.thesis: This is the only crowded theme in the upper ranks that ALSO has a 'trend' hurst tag (not mixed) and a strong durability_bar (0.76) plus high breadth (0.90). The crowding flag (z=1.82) is a size-down caution ONLY, never a fade — so I lean with the confirmed trend but with humility, and explicitly do not treat it as a buy because it is #3.
theses.dissent: Crowding z=1.82 is the highest in the ranks; per the guardrails, crowding marks tops/extension and the only validated response is to cap exposure — an overweight lean on the most crowded name is the closest thing here to reflexivity risk.

falsifier.text: CIBR breaks below its 50-day average and breadth drops below 0.7 before 20 days elapse.

theses.subject: Financials (Equal-Weight)
theses.thesis: Ranks 29th (score -0.345) with a 'trend' hurst tag but near-zero breadth (0.079) — a trend in almost no constituents. This is the weakest breadth/trend combination among eligible non-crowded names, and there is no crowding flag to excuse the collapse. A relative underweight is a direction, not a size, and is the most honest expression of where leadership is NOT concentrating.
theses.dissent: Equal-weight sector exposures can lag cap-weight momentum but still grind higher in a broad risk-on tape; narrow breadth in a trend-tag name can also just mean the trend is driven by a couple of mega-banks, which is not a bearish signal per se.

falsifier.text: XLF breadth recovers above 0.5 and score climbs into positive territory before 30 days.

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
